headline: Tesla has renamed its "Full Self-Driving (Supervised)" driver-assistance software "Tesla Assisted Driving" in Europe after Germany's transport minister called the old name somewhat misleading.
score_reason: Viral floor 7: 22 outlets carry it (VIRAL RULE)
importance_line: The change matters to drivers in Europe, then to regulators and Tesla, because the new name says more plainly that the driver must stay in charge and Germany's transport minister now backs approval of the renamed system; the doubt is that approval still depends on an EU-wide vote that could come later this year.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Tesla has renamed its "Full Self-Driving (Supervised)" software "Tesla Assisted Driving" in Europe after Steffen Bilger, Germany's transport minister, said the old name was somewhat misleading because the software does not do the whole job of driving; a ministry release says Tesla itself proposed the change after talks last month. Bilger, whose call for EU-wide approval we reported on 7 Oct 2026, says he will now argue for the renamed system before an EU-wide vote that could come later this year; that day we also carried a Reuters report that Tesla had pressed hard for European approval.
notes: Update of our 7 Oct 2026 edition (Reuters: Tesla pressed EU officials hard to approve FSD). Read TechCrunch only; CNBC returned HTTP 403. The rename rests on the German ministry's release as relayed by TechCrunch. machine_action false: the story is a rename and a regulatory step, not a machine shown working. Score kept at the viral floor of 7.
